runNote: Stress-test the supervisor-selected fixture verdicts dated 2026-10-11 on the real board; selected answers are not a substitute for returned board feedback.

cards.title: Needed is independent of stock
cards.body: Keep the needed mark as an independent household shopping decision, even when a supply is already present; never infer it from quantities or stock levels.
cards.tests: “The household controls that mark as a shopping decision.”
cards.why: Accepting supports restocking preferences and the explicit exclusion of stock accounting. Resisting could make the shopping list closer to the brief’s phrase “what is missing”, but would need a separate definition of absence and risks introducing stock semantics.

cards.title: Reuse equivalent names; preserve fully named variants
cards.body: Trim supplied names and compare them case-insensitively. Adding “ rice ” after “Rice” reuses the existing item without changing its needed mark. “Brown rice” and “White rice” remain distinct because their full supplied names differ.
cards.tests: “Names should let the household recognise its supplies without accidental duplication.”
cards.why: Accepting prevents accidental duplicate shopping entries while allowing explicitly named variants. Resisting preserves every spelling as a separate entry and avoids implicit identity matching, but puts duplicate cleanup on the household.

cards.title: Continue the session with visible unsaved changes
cards.body: If local storage saving fails, keep the session usable and expose unsaved changes. Never claim reload retention until saving succeeds.
cards.tests: “A storage problem must not make the current session unusable or imply that unsaved changes will survive a reload.”
cards.why: Accepting lets the household continue useful work with an honest persistence limit. Resisting and blocking edits would avoid accumulating unsaved work, but would make a storage failure prevent the household from using the current session.
